Hi Ava —

Appreciate the clear list. I've attached a draft capability matrix (redwood_scim_admin_matrix.xlsx) and a high-level 5-week rollout plan. Highlights below; the attachments contain the full mapping and examples you can share with security.

Quick answers (summary):
- SCIM: Full SCIM v2 support. PUT + PATCH supported; our default connector uses PATCH for incremental updates to minimize churn. We also provide a bulk-sync endpoint for initial population (CSV import or SCIM bulk operation).
- Conflict resolution: Last-write-wins at the attribute level by default; we offer optional conflict hooks so customers can inject custom resolution logic during onboarding.
- Multi-tenant namespaces: Customers may opt-in to tenant-scoped usernames or global UID namespace. We recommend tenant-scoped UIDs for overlapping usernames.
- Rate limits: Default per-tenant SCIM rate limit is 250 requests/min; we can raise this for enterprise with a negotiated SLA.
- SSO: We support SAML 2.0 and OIDC (RP and IdP flows). Out-of-the-box claim/attribute mappings include email, name, groups, and role claims. Custom attribute mapping supported via the Console or API.
- Delegated admin: Role-based RBAC with built-in admin roles (Tenant Admin, User Manager, Read-Only Auditor). All admin actions are logged and exportable via the Audit API.

Attachments included: redwood_scim_admin_matrix.xlsx (matrix + examples), project_plan_v1.pdf (5-week rollout with milestones), scim_matrix.csv (sample mapping export).

Next steps: If the attachments look good, can we schedule a 30-minute technical walk-through with your IAM engineer this week? I'll loop Kim and Marissa to cover deep SCIM and provisioning questions.

Hi Ava —

Following on Connor's summary, a few technical clarifications that will help your IAM team validate the integration:

- PATCH semantics: Our PATCH follows RFC 7644; we accept replace/add/remove operations. We also expose a dry-run parameter for bulk sync so you can validate transforms before committing.
- Bulk import: For initial provisioning at scale (>100k users) we recommend the CSV import combined with the bulk-sync job; it creates a job id so you can query progress and reconcile failures.
- Group membership / nested groups: We support groups and nested groups; group membership is reflected both as SCIM multi-valued attributes and as a separate groups endpoint.
- Rate limiting and backoff: We return standard 429 with Retry-After. For heavy syncs we can provision a temporary rate-limit increase window.
- Delegated admin audit: Audit entries include actor id, timestamp, action, target resource, and request payload hash. Audit logs are exportable via our Console and retained per your retention settings (default 90 days; enterprise options up to 7 years).

I've put a couple of sample SCIM PATCH payloads into the matrix file and annotated the project plan with estimated service windows for the pilot cutover. If HelixWare has any compliance-specific retention or proof-of-change requirements (e.g., signed change approvals), flag them and we'll include in the runbook.

Ava / Darren / Procurement —

Thanks — answers below and next steps included. I've also forwarded our Legal team's initial redlines for the SOW for your counsel to review (redlines_lgl.docx).

1) Rate limits: Yes, rate limits are enforced per-tenant by default. Burst concurrency is soft-capped — by default the system will allow short bursts up to 500 concurrent SCIM requests for a few seconds; sustained concurrency beyond 250 requests/minute will be throttled unless we provision an elevated SLA window. We can include a temporary elevated window during the pilot cutover (recommended 4-hour window).

2) Audit export: Attached sample export (scim_matrix.csv was a sample attribute export; separate sample JSON audit export included in the matrix workbook). Fields that are masked by default: user password hash, tenant API key, and any attributes marked as PII by your policy; actor and action are never masked. We can provide a redactable field list for your compliance team.

3) SOW / procurement: We can accept a 12-month initial term with net-45. I'll ask our RevOps to prepare the SOW addendum; I've attached the legal redlines (redlines_lgl.docx) and the draft project plan (project_plan_v1.pdf). If those are acceptable, please send a PO or trigger the DocuSign link you referenced and I'll route internally for countersignature.

- Week 0: Legal & SOW sign-off; provide dev/test API keys (1 business day after countersignature).
- Week 1: Pilot provisioning (up to 2k users), SCIM dry-run and group sync test.
- Week 2: Pilot validation, security review, audit export verification.
- Week 3: Production migration window (4-hour elevated throughput window).
- Week 4–5: Post-migration follow-up, tuned rate limits, and knowledge transfer.
